title: Earned value
intro: EV always comes first in the formulas. A negative variance or an index below 1.0 is bad news.

entries.name: Earned value
entries.reading: The budgeted value of the work actually done

entries.name: Cost variance
entries.reading: Negative: over budget. Positive: under budget.

entries.name: Schedule variance
entries.reading: Negative: behind schedule. Positive: ahead.

entries.name: Cost performance index
entries.reading: Below 1.0: over budget. Above 1.0: under budget.

entries.name: Schedule performance index
entries.reading: Below 1.0: behind schedule. Above 1.0: ahead.

entries.name: Estimate at completion, performance continues
entries.reading: The most common forecast. Use it when a question gives no hint.

entries.name: Estimate at completion, one-time variance
entries.reading: The remaining work goes as planned

entries.name: Estimate at completion, cost and schedule both count
entries.reading: Both cost and schedule performance affect the remaining work

entries.name: Estimate to complete
entries.reading: Still to be spent

entries.name: Variance at completion
entries.reading: Negative: expected to finish over budget

entries.name: To-complete performance index
entries.reading: Work remaining ÷ funds remaining. Below 1.0 is good: the rest is easier than planned.

title: Schedule
intro: The critical path formulas here start the project on day 1, as the lesson does. Courses that start on day 0 drop the − 1 and + 1.

entries.name: Three-point estimate, triangular
entries.reading: Simple average of optimistic, most likely and pessimistic

entries.name: Three-point estimate, beta (PERT)
entries.reading: Weighted average: the most likely value counts four times

entries.name: Parametric estimate
entries.formula: Quantity × time per unit, or quantity ÷ rate
entries.reading: A rate from historical data applied to the quantity of work

entries.name: Early finish (forward pass)
entries.reading: The earliest an activity can finish
entries.section: The forward pass: early start and early finish

entries.name: Late start (backward pass)
entries.reading: The latest an activity can start without delaying the project
entries.section: The backward pass: late start and late finish

entries.name: Total float
entries.formula: Total float = LS − ES = LF − EF
entries.reading: Zero on the critical path. If the two results differ, recheck the passes.

entries.name: Communication channels
entries.reading: n is the number of people. Count the project manager.

entries.name: Risk score
entries.reading: The highest scores get attention first

entries.name: Expected monetary value
entries.reading: Add it to the base cost to compare options

entries.name: Average velocity
entries.reading: A planning aid for the team that produced it, not a target

entries.name: Iterations remaining
entries.formula: Points left in the backlog ÷ velocity
entries.reading: How many more iterations the remaining work needs

entries.name: Weighted shortest job first
entries.formula: WSJF = cost of delay ÷ job size
entries.reading: The highest score goes first

entries.name: Lead time and cycle time
entries.formula: Lead time: request to delivery. Cycle time: start of work to finish.
entries.reading: Lead time includes the waiting before work starts
